findings.title: Processing renamed auxiliary XML bypasses XML depth limits
findings.summary: A DOCX author can put deeply nested auxiliary XML under a non-.xml/.rels suffix. Admission drains those bytes without XML policy, while rendering, revision listing, revision acceptance/rejection and comparison follow internal relationships and recursively build a DOM. Confirmed rendering parts include theme, styles, numbering, comments/commentsExtended, notes and headers/footers; get_revisions and comparison also parse renamed footnotes/endnotes. A small admitted package can terminate the native host or trap WASM. The assigned source additionally confirms eager relationship-selected fontTable parsing before font inspection, including renamed fontTable.bin. Comparison preprocessing also follows renamed styles and charts, alongside footnotes/endnotes. The assigned Standard source additionally identifies edit initialization's existing_comment_ids on relationship-selected comments before the later checked CommentFamily loader. Assigned discovery-0019 corroborates the same shared selector for styles, theme, numbering and fontTable under .bin names; its proof is limited to those four consumers, while earlier validated consumer paths remain retained. Assigned discovery-0027 additionally confirms relationship-selected settings bytes reaching settings_dom/settings_dom_xml and unchecked DOM construction on cache miss; settings is now a supplied validated consumer, whereas earlier recommendations remain historical source limitations. Assigned discovery-0028 supplies already-validated linked-textbox and diagram consumers: relationship-ID media targets at src/convert/mod.rs:17417-17428 and :17453-17464 are decoded and recursively parsed regardless of filename. The new source corroborates fontTable, theme, styles, numbering, settings, comments, notes and header/footer paths, and records that admission's content-type check covers the main part only. Assigned discovery-0031 additionally preserves strict normalization's extension-based pass-through: a relationship-selected fonts.bin remains unmodified before eager fontTable parsing. The raw unchecked parser's documented caller obligations are not themselves the finding.
findings.remediation: Apply active InputLimits at a centralized checked XML access/parse boundary for every semantic XML consumer regardless of filename, or resolve/classify and admit XML through actual content-type/relationship use. Cover theme, styles, numbering, converter comments/commentsExtended, notes and headers/footers; explicitly cover the now supplied validated settings_dom/settings_dom_xml cache-miss consumer, with earlier settings-only recommendations retained as historical source limitations. Preserve renamed-main checks, and enforce actual DOM construction depth or use iterative construction. Apply that same mandatory checked boundary to get_revisions and comparison notes parsing, including both footnotes and endnotes; propagate typed refusal under the active comparer InputLimits. Include pre_process_markup's relationship-selected notes at src/document_comparer.rs:4725-4750 and exposed Python get_revisions_json/WASM getRevisions; valid arbitrary part names remain supported. Include linked-textbox and diagram relationship targets in the mandatory filename-independent checked XML boundary before parse_xdocument and in regression coverage. These are now supplied validated affected consumers from discovery-0028; earlier sources' proposed-only status remains historical. Cover revision_processor RevisionIds collection and process_part for all six selected auxiliary buckets (headers, footers, endnotes, footnotes, comments and styles), including public revision acceptance/rejection. Explicitly include the now-confirmed fontTable loader (src/convert/font_table.rs:66-78; src/convert/mod.rs:806) in the mandatory checked XML boundary; parsing must be bounded before any font root/entry inspection. Explicitly cover comparison defined_style_ids (src/document_comparer.rs:4684-4696), relationship-selected footnotes/endnotes (4724-4750) and chart preprocessing (4861-4878), all reached through admitted nonidentical comparison inputs (6555-6569,6607-6625). Apply the same mandatory XML boundary before edit initialization's existing_comment_ids scan, not only in the later checked CommentFamily loader; preserve the effective checks at inspect::parse_part_within and edit::load_stories. Enforce the same checked boundary before settings DOM cache population, and preserve valid bounded nonstandard auxiliary filenames.

findings.title: WMF record-boundary failures amplify polygon work and retained text
findings.summary: Rendering a DOCX with a crafted placeable WMF lets short declared records consume payload from later records, which the outer parser then revisits. Polygon/polypolygon/polyline records can cause billions of coordinate decodes from roughly 512 KiB; EXTTEXTOUT/TEXTOUT records can retain hundreds of megabytes of overlapping owned strings from roughly 205.6 KB. The common missing record-local boundary bypasses the canvas cap and original package budgets. A further framing uses alternating six-byte EXTTEXTOUT and unknown 0xFFFF record headers to claim 65,535 text bytes from subsequent records, implying several GiB of retained strings from roughly 1 MiB of media; this is a static estimate. A supplied 7-word EXTTEXTOUT framing uses 65536 fourteen-byte records plus a 65535-byte suffix in less than 1 MiB and requests about 4 GiB of decoded characters; nonzero mapping dimensions and nonblank text are required. This is a static estimate. Assigned discovery-0031 supplies an additional static eight-byte TEXTOUT framing with a 65535-byte claimed string and overlapping following bytes. About 1 MiB can request multiple gigabytes of retained text; valid whole-file reads, nonblank text and nonzero mapping extents remain required. No out-of-bounds memory read is asserted.
findings.remediation: Confine every WMF handler, including field, font, string and geometry reads, to a slice limited to its checked declared record extent. Before allocation validate fixed fields, ring/point counts and coordinate arrays, EXTTEXTOUT options/optional rectangle and text count, and TEXTOUT padded string plus trailing coordinates against that slice using checked arithmetic. Refuse inconsistent records before decoding/rasterization/replay and enforce cumulative decoded-text, record and total geometry/work budgets. Keep the already bounded EMF behavior.

findings.title: Metadata scrub leaves property parts under alternate names
findings.summary: With docprops enabled, scrub removes metadata only from three conventional filenames. A document using alternate package relationship targets can retain creators, editors, dates, company/manager or custom properties while scrub returns success. The custom-properties branch additionally skips relationship/content-type removal when docProps/custom.xml is absent, leaving an active relationship to a relocated target such as metadata/private.xml.
findings.remediation: Resolve all core, extended and custom property parts through authoritative package relationships and content types, sanitize every applicable internal target according to docprops selection, and remove corresponding custom-property parts/relationships/content-type records coherently. Verify the selected privacy postcondition; refuse unsupported or ambiguous layouts rather than returning a successfully scrubbed copy. Preserve intentional title/subject/application and revision-date retention. Missing/invalid selected targets require explicit refusal or documented safe handling; default public and CLI callers must enforce the same postcondition. Include supported Strict property relationship variants and regression cases containing both conventional and relocated targets; every active property target must satisfy the requested postcondition.

findings.title: Repeated HTML chunk references bypass conversion memory budgets
findings.summary: A DOCX can repeatedly reference one modest HTML part. The renderer admits the small original package, then copies and converts that chunk separately for every reference and concatenates all generated XML. The resulting allocation and work can exceed package budgets by orders of magnitude. For example, 10,000 short references to one 1 MiB ordinary HTML paragraph can imply roughly 10 GiB of generated XML; this is a static estimate, not a runtime measurement. The assigned source also supplies nested HTML tables as a depth variant of this post-admission expansion boundary: generated WML enters unchecked DOM and recursive table layout. Complete repair must enforce both cumulative size/work and generated depth; the earlier dedicated depth record remains cross-referenced.
findings.remediation: Make altChunk expansion fallible under active cumulative expanded-byte, node/element, depth, work and occurrence budgets. Check contributions before conversion/allocation/append, including repeated internal relationships and MIME-decoded chunks, and validate generated XML under active limits before DOM construction. Caching may reduce repeated conversion CPU but cannot replace the total-output budget.

findings.title: Cyclic Markdown drawing dependencies terminate conversion through unbounded recursion
findings.summary: A drawing: image destination in ordinary Markdown is base64-decoded and deserialized into a dependency graph without validation. Package materialization recursively follows each dep.rels.part before writing the dependent part and has no active-node or completed-node map. A one-node self-reference causes indefinite recursion and stack exhaustion, even with default Markdown conversion options and no image loader. Header/footer drawing payloads also reach this same materializer through view_stories::story_part. Capture memoizes a part before descending, so even capture-produced envelopes can encode a cycle; capture count/byte limits do not establish an acyclic imported graph. The supplied discovery-0030 trace additionally records that an empty boxes collection bypasses text-box-specific Writer finish checks; these checks do not validate the dependency graph.
findings.remediation: Validate dependency indices, count/byte/depth limits and graph shape at import. Materialize with an active/completed traversal state and index-to-output map, rejecting cycles or reserving identities to support cycles without recursive expansion. Memoize shared subgraphs. Enforce explicit dependency-edge and traversal-work budgets before assembly; when rejecting active-node revisits return a typed conversion refusal. Apply the same graph validation and traversal state to header/footer drawing materialization, not only body drawings.

findings.title: Public Strict-format probe inflates unbounded document headers
findings.summary: The public main_part_is_strict helper reads word/document.xml without admission or an inflation/preamble cap. A compressible oversized/unfinished root opening tag or long XML comment keeps the last '<' at offset zero; the full growing head remains retained and is repeatedly scanned until the root tag completes or EOF, allowing memory/CPU exhaustion for direct library consumers. The assigned audit establishes direct public-library exposure and found no in-repository production caller; ordinary rendering is not claimed to call this detector.
findings.remediation: Apply bounded admission before indexing/inflation and explicit cumulative inflated-byte/preamble/work limits to this public helper. Use a streaming lexical probe with bounded retained state for comments, declarations and chunk-spanning root tags; refuse excessive probes with a checked/limited API and safe default limits.

findings.title: Rendering an admitted DOCX can retain gigabytes of duplicate embedded fonts
findings.summary: Distinct font-table aliases may all reference one embedded font part. Rendering eagerly loads every alias, copies the full font and retains a separate buffer for each name, multiplying a small admitted package into gigabytes of memory even if its body never uses those fonts. Assigned discovery-0031 corroborates distinct invented family names bypassing known-catalogue exclusions; valid Face::parse results and the later u16 face-index limit do not bound earlier alias copies.
findings.remediation:
Cache decoded font buffers by resolved package part and effective obfuscation key, share Arc values across aliases, and enforce an aggregate decoded-font allocation/work budget before copying.
Enforce face-count limits before decoding/retention and load only used faces where possible; cover all four style slots and different effective keys.

findings.title: Unbounded document table spans exhaust memory during rendering
findings.summary: Untrusted direct OOXML gridSpan/gridBefore/gridAfter and imported HTML/MHT colspan values become unrestricted output column counts. Tiny metadata can request a billion columns, driving dense column/preference/merge vectors or pre-DOM gridCol XML generation before derived-output budgets. These independently reachable paths require controls before both import generation and layout; package byte/depth admission does not bound their semantic expansion.
findings.remediation: Enforce practical per-cell span/row-skip and checked cumulative table/grid/output budgets across direct OOXML gridSpan/gridBefore/gridAfter and HTML/MHT colspan. Apply the common limit before HTML generation and before RawCell, column/preference/merge allocation or span-sized work; use checked sums and col+span arithmetic and return a typed conversion refusal. Neither importer-only nor later layout-only checking is sufficient. Use fallible allocation/reservation within those bounds so capacity failures become typed refusals. Carry the caller-configurable column/occupancy budget through every table source and enforce a generated-XML/output ceiling before altChunk materialization.

findings.title: Repeated relationship IDs trigger quadratic repair work
findings.summary: Opening a package repairs identical duplicate relationship IDs. For n distinct IDs each repeated identically, each repair linearly searches an increasingly long Vec, producing quadratic CPU work on shallow metadata that fits existing byte and attribute limits. Assigned discovery-0031 supplies approximately 200000 shallow Relationship records with 100000 distinct identical duplicate pairs within a 64 MiB part, implying about five billion membership comparisons. Conflicting duplicates remain promptly refused; counts are static.
findings.remediation: Track already-reported duplicate IDs in a HashSet or alongside seen-map state, retaining a Vec only for deterministic reporting order. Optionally cap relationship-record/work totals before repair; test many distinct identical duplicate pairs while preserving deterministic repaired-ID order and conflicting-duplicate refusals. Apply an active relationship-record/work budget at metadata admission in addition to making duplicate membership near-linear.

findings.title: Entity decoding repeatedly scans the input suffix
findings.summary: HTML altChunk text with bare ampersands and the public XML entity decoder repeatedly search the remaining suffix for ';', yielding quadratic CPU work. A valid admitted .rels Target containing repeated & is normalized upstream and redundantly decoded by PartFs, reaching the same XML sink during rendering, inspection, revision processing or comparison even when the target part does not exist. An additional admitted-main-XML route uses an unquoted value whose first character never reappears: the DOM consumes through EOF and decodes a bare-ampersand comment as an attribute, reaching the same quadratic XML decoder. Ordinary bare-ampersand text is rejected upstream and is not this proof. The same HTML decoder is also reached by Markdown-to-DOCX raw HTML blocks and attribute values; its ten-byte accepted-entity bound is applied after the unbounded search. Assigned discovery-0031 corroborates both established decoders independently: ordinary HTML/MHT paragraph text reaches the HTML helper even when script/style content is skipped, while an internal fontTable target reaches redundant XML decoding before any absent-part lookup. Its supplied offline dependency evidence identifies oxml-opc 0.14.2 and quick-xml 0.41.0 attribute normalization, independently supported by the repository target round-trip test. No reducer dependency inspection occurred.
findings.remediation: Scan entities once without revisiting suffixes. In HTML, bound the search to the supported entity-length window before looking for ';'; give XML decoding a monotonic parser or bounded entity grammar. Remove PartFs's redundant relationship decoding when upstream supplies normalized attributes; retain the linear XML-helper repair for its other callers and the separate bounded HTML-helper repair. Preserve canonical literal '&' part names and one-time entity normalization through round trips. Preserve the standalone XML helper's documented permissive output for unsupported or unterminated references while making its work linear. Apply practical relationship-target length/work bounds as defense in depth, preserving exactly one normalization pass and the standalone helper's linear permissive behavior. Align admission/DOM attribute token boundaries or reject unsupported unquoted syntax as defense in depth. Preserve the linear XML decoder fix for this comment-to-attribute route; removing only the redundant relationship decode does not cover it. Apply the bounded HTML helper consistently to Markdown raw-HTML block text and attribute consumers, using UTF-8-safe bounded lookahead and preserving recognized entities, malformed literal retention and multibyte text.

findings.title: Redaction postcondition misses confidential phrases split across DrawingML runs
findings.summary: The final leak check joins WordprocessingML run text but checks DrawingML chart text only one node at a time. A phrase split between adjacent chart-title runs survives a successful body redaction and remains recoverable from both output packages. The corroborating source includes preserved chart/diagram DrawingML a:p/a:r/a:t subpaths and downstream Office rendering; disclosure still requires sharing the result.
findings.remediation: Extend leak detection to logical text of supported components, including DrawingML paragraphs/chart rich text, aligning with extraction logic. Add a body-redaction regression with matching split chart-title text and require refusal for both output packages. Include preserved diagram paragraphs as well as chart-title rich text, and fail closed when a supported text-bearing structure cannot be inspected.

findings.title: Streaming XML hash repeatedly rescans growing escaped opening tags
findings.summary: HashXmlBuf searches the entire accumulated opening tag for > after every emitted fragment. Escaped attribute values emit one fragment per character; retained custom-namespace paragraph attributes select this fallback hashing path, causing quadratic CPU consumption within admitted XML sizes.
findings.remediation: Search only the new fragment for the root-tag terminator or expose explicit tag-completion state from serialization. Preserve linear behavior for escaped values and test large retained custom attributes through public comparison.

findings.title: Nested semantic fields multiply retained instructions and hash work
findings.summary: Field salting copies each instruction into every open semantic field and materializes the full chain again for every atom. Sibling fldChar begin/end markers can create arbitrarily deep field nesting at shallow XML depth, amplifying a modest instruction into gigabytes.
findings.remediation: Bound semantic field depth and total instruction/hash work before copying. Use shared instruction representations and incremental/compositional field hashes instead of materializing every full nested code chain; return a typed refusal when budgets are exceeded.
